scenario: AITA for reducing my tip to compensate for a drink I didn’t order? (US) | So short story, at a restaurant today for lunch I got an entree and a glass of water (not fancy water mind you, just tap and it didn’t even have ice). My girlfriend got the same entree and a tea. When the cheque came we had been charged the same amount, $10 for the entree and $2 for a “beverage”. When I pointed this out to the waitress she said water was a beverage and I needed to pay for it. When it came time to tip time I did the math for what I would usually tip, $2.50 tip for my $10 entree and then subtracted the price of the $2 tap water. Basically I left a .50 cent tip. My girlfriend thinks it was an asshole move and I think I’m not paying $2 for lukewarm tap water. basically I brought my cheque total to the $12.50 it would have originally been without the water added.

prediction.raw: I would say: 1 (You are the asshole). As a neutral AI, I can understand your frustration about being charged for tap water, which is typically complimentary in many restaurants. However, reducing your tip to compensate for the drink you didn't order may not be the most fair or reasonable approach. Tips are typically given to show appreciation for the service provided by the wait staff, and reducing the tip in this case may unfairly penalize the waitress for a policy that is not her decision. It's possible that the restaurant has a policy of charging for all beverages, including water, and the waitress was simply following that policy. A more constructive approach might have been to politely speak with the manager or waitress about the issue and express your concerns about being charged for tap water. This could have led to a resolution or a compromise, such as the restaurant waiving the charge for the water or offering a complimentary beverage in the future. By reducing your tip, you may have inadvertently affected the waitress's income, which could be seen as unfair and unreasonable. Hence, the "asshole" label.
